text:
lara: Customer reports 401s from an embedded webview. They say console shows no request id, only a timestamped error screenshot. asking if we can escalate for a repro.

sam_support: thanks — can you ask them to send a couple quick things so eng can triage?
- full curl or HAR (if non-dev, a screenshot of network panel is OK)
- SDK console logs from the time of the failure (js/android/ios)
- exact local time and timezone when the error happened
- any proxy or gateway they sit behind (CDN, mobile-proxy)

customer_acme: i can get a screenshot and the network panel. not sure how to produce a curl from our webview though.

sam_support: no problem. smallest set we need: 1) any request header that looks like a request/ref or trace id (examples: x-request-id, x-redwood-req, x-rw-reqref) 2) the full response body & status 3) the SDK session id shown in the console (if using redwood-js it prints "sessionRef" on init)

jun_engineer: quick troubleshooting note for them to follow (paste this in the thread):

> If you can run a quick capture: open DevTools -> Network. Reproduce the 401 and right-click the failing request -> Copy -> Copy as cURL. Paste the cURL here.
>
> If the webview blocks DevTools, please paste the error timestamp + a screenshot of the network logs and the top 30 lines of the browser console.
>
> For JS SDK: look for a console line like: `Redwood SDK init sessionRef=abc123` or `sessionRef: abc123`. That value helps correlate the request even if headers get stripped.

sam_support: include this curl example so they know what to send (remove secrets before posting):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "X-Request-Ref: <REQREF>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

lara: also ask them to generate a debug bundle from the console if possible — Console -> Sessions -> click session -> Export -> share link. That contains the session metadata + proto traces we can ingest.

customer_acme: ok i grabbed a cURL and the console log. but the headers look weird, our proxy might be rewriting them. what else helps if headers are stripped?

jun_engineer: if headers are stripped, the sessionRef / SDK session id is usually enough. Also send:
- timestamp (exact wallclock) + timezone
- the raw request body and response body (copy/paste)
- mobile: sysdiagnose or device logs around that timestamp; Android logcat or iOS device console often shows a `req_hash` or `session=<hex>` printed by the SDK

sam_support: 👍 If they cannot get a cURL or HAR, ask them to: 1) open Console -> SDK -> Network requests (or the equivalent in your app debug UI) 2) copy the failing request's request-id / sessionRef / correlation id and the response code and body 3) attach a short note: "timestamp, app version, sdk version, env (prod/staging), proxy/CDN"

deploy-bot: [automated] new support escalation created #5201234567 -> assigned to jun_engineer

jun_engineer: i'll take this one. once they post the sessionRef + cURL/har i'll correlate with our edge logs and either find the exact request or confirm header strip. If we can't find the req, we'll ask for a debug bundle link so we can pull the trace from their session.

customer_acme: posted cURL (redacted) and console screenshot. sessionRef=sr_9b8f

sam_support: received — thanks! will loop in eng and get back with next steps. :eyes:
